tasks.objective: Move process handling into src/session/ as a SessionExecutorFactory that creates SessionExecutors which run one agent process and return a SessionResult classifying process- and adapter-level outcomes, replacing src/session.ts and the process/adapter half of runner.ts's classification.
completion_criteria: A SessionExecutorFactory created with an AbortSignal, an optional timeout in seconds and an optional termination grace period produces SessionExecutors that all use that same signal, timeout and grace period. A unit test shows this for at least two executors created from one factory.

SessionExecutor.execute, given a prompt, a cwd and an optional model and effort: spawns the adapter's executable with the adapter's arguments in that cwd; writes the prompt to stdin; captures stdout; keeps the last 20 stderr lines, including an unterminated final line; gives the adapter a fresh temp output-file path and removes the temp directory afterwards; escalates SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGKILL at the grace interval on timeout or abort; does not spawn when the signal is already aborted; and gets the final message from the adapter.

SessionResult is a discriminated union with exactly these kinds: launch failed, timed out, interrupted, exited unsuccessfully, missing final message, invalid final message, success. Classification order is signal, then agent-reported error, then non-zero exit, then adapter-invalid, then missing. Unit tests pin each kind and each precedence case.

Failure kinds carry today's detail text: 'failed to launch agent: <message>'; 'agent exited unsuccessfully with signal <S>'; 'agent exited unsuccessfully (agent reported an error: <d>)' when the exit code is 0, otherwise 'agent exited unsuccessfully with exit code <n> (agent reported an error: <d>)'; 'agent exited unsuccessfully with exit code <n>'; 'agent final response is invalid: <reason>'; 'agent exited without a final response'. Every kind except launch failed, timed out and interrupted (success included) carries the stderr tail. Launch failed carries none.

Unit tests for SessionExecutorFactory, SessionExecutor and SessionResult classification live in test/unit/session/. src/session.ts and test/unit/session.test.ts are deleted, and none of their cases is lost.
Callers not migrated yet (runner.ts, src/cli.ts) consume the new SessionResult and factory. Stderr, exit codes and the stderr-tail rule are unchanged.

tasks.objective: Introduce the WorkflowStep interface, the CodingStep implementation and WorkflowStepResult in src/workflow/, so that nonce generation, session prompt assembly and result-block parsing sit in one place and every SessionResult or parsed block maps to a step outcome, replacing src/protocol.ts.
completion_criteria: Each time CodingStep executes, it generates a fresh nonce. It passes the SessionExecutor a session prompt equal to the launch prompt, a blank line, '---', then code.md with every {{NONCE}} replaced by that nonce, then a trailing newline, byte-identical to today's buildSessionPrompt.
CodingStep parses only the last complete <afk-harness-result> block carrying its own nonce. Blocks with another nonce and echoed examples are ignored.

WorkflowStepResult outcomes are Continue (repeat), Finished (complete), StepFailed (fail, failure summary), Blocked (blocked, blocker text), SessionFailed (launch failed, exited unsuccessfully, missing or invalid final message, or contract violation), Timeout and Interrupted. task_id and task_plan_file are carried as parsed. Unit tests in test/unit/workflow/ pin every row of the AC-014 table using a stubbed SessionExecutor.

A contract violation yields SessionFailed with detail 'agent final response is invalid: <violation>' and the session's stderr tail. SessionFailed from a SessionResult carries that result's detail and stderr tail, with an empty tail for launch failed.

Every case in test/unit/protocol.test.ts and the classification and nonce cases in test/unit/runner.test.ts at commit 3f42e29 has an equivalent unit test at the step or session layer with identical detail text. The implementation notes record the mapping.

tasks.objective: Replace runner.ts and the formatting in reporter.ts with a WorkflowExecutor that applies today's run policy, publishes every WorkflowEvent from doc/ARCHITECTURE.md to WorkflowObservers and returns the terminal result, plus a ConsoleReporter in src/reporter/ that turns those events into today's exact [afk] stderr lines.
completion_criteria: WorkflowExecutor is created with WorkflowOptions (adapter, model, reasoning effort, max iterations, session timeout, cwd), a LaunchPrompt and a SessionExecutorFactory. It creates one SessionExecutor and one CodingStep per iteration.

Policy: Continue and StepFailed start the next iteration. Finished, Blocked, Timeout and Interrupted stop immediately. After a SessionFailed one retry is allowed; a second consecutive SessionFailed ends with WorkflowFailed. Any other outcome resets the allowance. Retries count toward the limit. A SessionFailed on the last iteration with no previous error ends with MaxIterationsReached.

Events are immutable values with a 'type' discriminator and the names WorkflowStarted, IterationStarted, StepExecutionStarted, StepExecutionFinished, StepExecutionFailed, StepExecutionBlocked, StepExecutionRetried, SessionExecutionErrorOccurred, IterationFinished, WorkflowFinished, WorkflowInterrupted, WorkflowBlocked, WorkflowFailed, WorkflowTimedOut and MaxIterationsReached, all spelled correctly. They are published in the order given in the design's 'Event sequence' section. On a retry iteration both IterationStarted and StepExecutionRetried are published.

run() returns the terminal event, and observers receive exactly one terminal event, the same one. Terminal events carry the data their reporting and exit code need: the iteration limit, failure detail and stderr tail, blocker text, the configured timeout in seconds, and task metadata.
Observers cannot change control flow: the executor ignores observer return values, and a unit test shows that an observer which mutates or returns values has no effect on the run.

test/unit/workflow/ uses a recording observer to cover the policy and the full event sequence for: complete; blocked; fail then complete; iteration limit; retry recovers; two consecutive session failures; timeout; interruption; and a session failure on the last iteration.

ConsoleReporter writes exactly today's lines to its injected sink: the iteration line for a non-retry IterationStarted; the retry line using the configured limit; 'Task failure: …'; 'Execution error: …' followed by each stderr-tail line; and the final status line for each terminal event, with none for WorkflowFailed. It writes nothing for any other event. test/unit/reporter/ pins every event's output.
src/reporter/ imports only workflow event and observer types and no node module that writes output. No other module in src/ writes run-time [afk] status lines.

EXIT_CODES, the exit-code help text and the mapping from terminal result to exit code (0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 130) move to src/cli/. src/runner.ts, src/reporter.ts, test/unit/runner.test.ts and test/unit/reporter.test.ts are deleted; every policy case in runner.test.ts at 3f42e29 has an equivalent in test/unit/workflow/.
src/cli.ts wires the WorkflowExecutor, subscribes a ConsoleReporter writing to stderr, and exits with the code for the result of run(). It no longer formats run-time status lines.
